_note: Shared worked-example data for FMS engineering item 10 part A (PLC program standard + complete device function-block library): guide docs/FMS system design/70_plc_library_A_standard_fbs.md (part A), PLC source tools/fmse/plc_lib/*.st, tools/fmse/*.py, web/fmse10*.js. Parts B (module programs M01-M22) and C (cell controller + virtual commissioning of the kit) follow. Guide, tools and web must give IDENTICAL results with the rules below. All values are EXAMPLES; real PLC code is written, reviewed, tested and signed off by qualified people; safety functions only in the F-program.

decisions.topic: Who clears the command request (data block word 3 bit0 CmdChangeRequest)
options: module clears CntrlCmd + CmdChangeRequest (item 9 teaching example)
cell controller clears it after it sees the new state (guide 66 H2.2)
4-phase echo handshake: CC sets, module echoes CmdAck/CmdRej, CC clears, module clears echo
decisions.rule: One writer per word: words 0-1, 4, 6-11, 16-18 are written ONLY by the module, words 2-3, 5, 12-15, 19 ONLY by the cell controller. CC writes CntrlCmd + sets CmdChangeRequest in ONE FC16 write. Module: on the RISING edge of CmdChangeRequest evaluate the command (state + mode table of item 5) -> Status.Bits bit8 CmdAck (accepted, command executed in the same scan) or bit9 CmdRej (rejected, Admin.WarningNo = module*1000 + 900 + command). CC: on CmdAck or CmdRej clear CmdChangeRequest (and CntrlCmd = 0). Module: when CmdChangeRequest is FALSE clear CmdAck and CmdRej. CC time-out 2 s without echo -> communication alarm. A new command needs a new rising edge (no command is executed twice).
decisions.why: Modbus/OPC UA have no 'write-once' semantics; if both sides write the same word, a late write of one side can erase the other's (race). The echo makes the result (accepted / rejected) visible and gives a clean 4-phase handshake like item 6.

options: local codes per module (10, 11, 12 ...) as in item 9
decisions.rule: AlarmNo = M x 1000 + 10 x i + a, M = module number (M02 -> 2), i = instance number of the device FB in the module expansion order of item 8 (1..99, only instances with an FB), a = local alarm code of the FB (1..9); module-level alarms (sequence, homing, communication) use i = 0 (M x 1000 + 1..9) and 900 + n for command rejections (warnings). Example: APC01 (M02) instance 1 'Rotate' (FB_Valve2) alarm 1 'did not reach end position' -> 2011. INT range is enough (M22 -> 22999). Guide 66 '4 digits' becomes '4-5 digits'.
decisions.why: The number alone tells module type, device and fault; the alarm text table is generated from the library (item 10B), identical in PLC, HMI and cell controller.

decisions.topic: Reaction to clamp pressure low (and every other alarm)
options: by ALARM CLASS per alarm and phase
decisions.rule: Every alarm has a class: A = stop at once (PackML internal Abort: equipment or product at risk, e.g. clamp pressure LOST while the spindle cuts, drive fault, feedback lost while moving), B = controlled pause (internal Hold from Execute: the operator can fix it and continue, e.g. clamp pressure NOT REACHED during the clamping step, end position not reached at a step), C = warning only (no state change: filter dirty, UPS on battery, a rejected command). Clamp pressure: monitored with two different alarms: 'pressure not reached in the clamp step' (class B -> Held, operator re-seats the pallet, Unhold repeats the step) and 'pressure lost while clamped in a machining state' (class A -> Abort + feed hold over the coupling).
decisions.why: PackML: Held = internal condition the operator can clear and continue; Aborted = fault, the job is lost and needs Clear + Reset. The class decides it, not the device.

decisions.rule: Resetting runs a HOMING sequence: (1) all outputs to the defined home command, (2) every device FB must report its home position (xAtA / stopped / not busy) within its timeout, (3) no active class A/B alarm, (4) safety OK (F-program status). Only then SC -> Idle. A device that is between end positions is driven to its home position ONLY if the module is in a state where motion is allowed (guards closed, safety OK); else alarm 'not in home position' (class B, i = 0, a = 1) and the module stays in Resetting until homed or Stop/Abort. Abort and Stop never move a device - they only switch outputs to the fail-safe value (de-energise) - so Resetting is the place where the module returns to a known state.
decisions.why: Item 9 scenarios B and E showed Idle with the rotation half-way - the next Start would begin from an unknown position. Homing in Resetting makes Idle mean 'ready and in a known position'.

_rules.common: tick = 100 ms = the cycle of the test bench (in a real PLC the FB runs in the 10 ms main task - only the time base changes). Every FB is called exactly once per tick. Inputs are persistent: an event '<tick> name=value' changes an input BEFORE the call of that tick. Edges (xReset, xRequest, xHornAck, xPb, xCmdChangeRequest) are detected inside the FB: e = x AND NOT x_prev (x_prev starts FALSE). Times: a counter n counts calls; a time is reached when n*100 >= t_ms. Log: tick 0 = 'init' with all outputs after the first call; then one line per tick listing only the outputs whose value changed (BOOL as 1/0, numbers as integers or shortest decimal). The ST source in tools/fmse/plc_lib/ implements exactly these rules with the same names.
_rules.FB_Sensor: debounce: if xOn <> xValue: cnt += 1 ; if cnt*100 >= (tOn_ms if xOn else tOff_ms): xValue = xOn, cnt = 0 ; else cnt = 0. Outputs xValue (init FALSE).
_rules.FB_Valve: FB_Valve1 (single solenoid, spring return: qSol TRUE -> position B) and FB_Valve2 (double solenoid, bistable: qSolA / qSolB). Inputs xPosA, xPosB (end switches), xCmdB (TRUE = go to / stay at B, FALSE = A), xEnable (FALSE = outputs off: Valve1 springs back to A, Valve2 HOLDS its position), xReset. cfg tMove_ms 2000, tLost_ms 300, tBoth_ms 200. Order: rst = edge(xReset) ; atA = xPosA AND NOT xPosB ; atB = xPosB AND NOT xPosA ; reached = atB if xCmdB else atA ; (1) if xError and rst and NOT (xPosA AND xPosB): xError = FALSE, iAlarm = 0, moving = NOT reached, n = 0, nl = 0 (retry) ; (2) if xCmdB <> prevCmd (prevCmd starts 'none' -> TRUE at the first call): moving = TRUE, n = 0 ; (3) nb = nb+1 if xPosA AND xPosB else 0 ; (4) if NOT xError: if nb*100 >= tBoth_ms: error, iAlarm 3 'both end switches on', moving = FALSE ; elif moving: nl = 0 ; if xEnable: n += 1 ; if reached: moving = FALSE elif n*100 >= tMove_ms: error, iAlarm 1 'end position not reached', moving = FALSE ; elif xEnable: nl = nl+1 if NOT reached else 0 ; if nl*100 >= tLost_ms: error, iAlarm 2 'left the end position without command' ; else nl = 0 ; (5) outputs: Valve1 qSol = xCmdB AND xEnable ; Valve2 qSolB = xCmdB AND xEnable, qSolA = NOT xCmdB AND xEnable (an error does NOT change the outputs - the module decides the reaction by alarm class) ; xAtA = atA ; xAtB = atB ; xBusy = moving AND NOT xError ; prevCmd = xCmdB.
_rules.FB_DriveSto: frequency inverter with STO (safe torque off is switched by the F-program; the standard program reads its F-copy xSto: TRUE = torque off). Inputs xReady, xFault (DI from the drive), xSto, xCmdRun, xReset. States 0 NOT READY, 1 READY, 2 RUNNING, 9 FAULT. Order: rst = edge(xReset) ; ack = FALSE ; if xFault and state <> 9: state 9, iAlarm 1 'drive fault' ; elif state 0: if xReady and NOT xSto: 1 ; elif state 1: if xSto or NOT xReady: 0 elif xCmdRun: 2 ; elif state 2: if xSto: 0 (STO is a normal safety stop, not a drive fault) elif NOT xReady: 9, iAlarm 3 'ready lost while running' elif NOT xCmdRun: 1 ; elif state 9: if rst and NOT xFault: 0, iAlarm 0, ack = TRUE. One transition per call. Outputs: iState ; xError = state = 9 ; xWarn = xCmdRun AND xSto (run requested while torque is off) ; wCtrl (control word to the drive over the bus) = (0 if xSto else 1) [bit0 ON/enable] + (2 if state = 2) [bit1 RUN] + (128 if ack) [bit7 fault acknowledge, one call].
_rules.FB_Heater: 2-point temperature control + monitoring. Inputs xOnFb (contactor auxiliary), xOverTemp (safety thermostat), rTemp, xTempGood (quality of the analog input FB), xEnable, rSp, xReset ; cfg rHyst 2.0, tFb_ms 500. Order: rst = edge ; (1) if xError and rst and NOT xOverTemp and (xTempGood or NOT xEnable) and NOT xOnFb: clear error, nfb = nw = 0 ; (2) if NOT xError: if xOverTemp: error iAlarm 1 'over-temperature (safety thermostat)' elif xEnable and NOT xTempGood: error iAlarm 3 'temperature signal bad' ; (3) heat: if NOT xEnable or xError: FALSE elif rTemp <= rSp - rHyst: TRUE elif rTemp >= rSp: FALSE (else unchanged) ; q = heat ; (4) nfb = nfb+1 if q and NOT xOnFb else 0 ; nw = nw+1 if NOT q and xOnFb else 0 ; if NOT xError and nfb*100 >= tFb_ms: error iAlarm 2 'no contactor feedback' ; if NOT xError and nw*100 >= tFb_ms: error iAlarm 4 'feedback without command (contactor welded?)' ; (5) if xError: heat = FALSE, q = FALSE ; qOn = q.
_rules.FB_PushButton: illuminated push-button. blink = (c // 5) MOD 2 = 0 with c = number of previous calls (1 Hz at 100 ms) ; qLamp = iLampMode = 1 OR (iLampMode = 2 AND blink) ; xClick = edge(xPb) ; xPressed = xPb.
_rules.FB_SignalTower: inputs iState (PackML state number), iAlarmClass (0 none, 1 A, 2 B, 3 C), xHornAck. blink as FB_PushButton. qRed = class 1 OR state in {8 Aborting, 9 Aborted} ; qYellow = class in {2,3} OR state in {2 Stopped, 5 Suspended, 11 Held} ; qGreen = state in {3,6,12,14,16} OR (state in {4 Idle, 17 Complete} AND blink) ; horn: if class in {1,2} and class <> previous class: horn = TRUE ; if edge(xHornAck) or class = 0: horn = FALSE ; qBuzzer = horn. Colours per IEC 60204-1 10.3 / IEC 60073 (red = danger/fault, yellow = abnormal/attention, green = normal; flashing green = ready, waiting).
_rules.FB_HandshakeHw: requester side of the hard-wired 4-phase handshake (item 8 HANDSHAKE_HW, item 6 logic). Inputs xReady, xBusy, xDone, xFault (from the partner), xStart, xReset ; cfg tHs_ms 2000, tJob_ms 10000. Order: rst = edge ; qReset = rst (one call, fault reset to the partner) ; xDoneOut = FALSE ; if xError: if rst and NOT xFault: clear error, step 0 ; elif xFault and step <> 0: error iAlarm 4 'partner fault' ; elif step 0: if xStart and xReady: 10, n = 0 ; elif 10: n += 1 ; if xBusy: 20, n = 0 elif n*100 >= tHs_ms: error iAlarm 1 'partner did not start (busy missing)' ; elif 20: n += 1 ; if xDone: 30, n = 0 elif n*100 >= tJob_ms: error iAlarm 2 'job time-out' ; elif 30: n += 1 ; if NOT xDone: 0, xDoneOut = TRUE elif n*100 >= tHs_ms: error iAlarm 3 'done not removed'. Outputs: iStep ; qRequest = qEnable = step in {10,20} AND NOT xError ; qAck = step = 30 AND NOT xError.
_rules.FB_Feeder: n = n+1 if NOT xSupplyOn else 0 ; xOk = xSupplyOn ; iAlarm = 1 'feeder breaker off' if n*100 >= tDelay_ms (200) else 0 (not latched, class C unless the module needs the supply).
_rules.FB_Ups: n = n+1 if xOnBattery else 0 ; xShutdownReq = n*100 >= tBuffer_ms (5000) ; iAlarm = 1 'UPS fault' if NOT xUpsOk else 2 'on battery' if xOnBattery else 0.
_rules.FB_Safe2Ch: diagnostic mirror of a 2-channel safety input (the safety function itself is in the F-program). Used by FB_Estop, FB_Door2Ch, FB_EnableSwitch, FB_LightCurtain (+ xWarn passed through), FB_SafetyCoupling (one for EstopIn, one for ZoneFree). Inputs xCh1, xCh2 (TRUE = safe/closed), xReset ; cfg tDisc_ms 500. latched starts TRUE (reset needed after power-on). Order: rst = edge ; nd = nd+1 if xCh1 <> xCh2 else 0 ; if nd*100 >= tDisc_ms and NOT xDiscErr: xDiscErr = TRUE, iAlarm 1 'discrepancy', bothOpen = FALSE ; if xDiscErr and NOT xCh1 and NOT xCh2: bothOpen = TRUE ; if NOT (xCh1 AND xCh2): latched = TRUE ; if rst and xCh1 and xCh2: (if xDiscErr and bothOpen: xDiscErr = FALSE, iAlarm 0) ; if NOT xDiscErr: latched = FALSE ; outputs xOk = xCh1 AND xCh2 AND NOT latched AND NOT xDiscErr ; xResetReq = latched AND xCh1 AND xCh2 AND NOT xDiscErr. A discrepancy can only be reset after BOTH channels were open (cross-fault test, as safety PLCs do).
_rules.FB_ModeSwitch: inputs xAuto, xMaint ; n = n+1 if xAuto AND xMaint else 0 ; iMode: Auto only -> 1 Production, Maint only -> 2 Maintenance, none -> 3 Manual, both -> unchanged ; xError = n*100 >= tDisc_ms (500) ; iAlarm = 1 if xError else 0. iMode init 3.
_rules.FB_Edm: external device monitoring (FB_ZoneOut, FB_ContactorPair: bInverted TRUE - NC mirror contacts are TRUE when the contactors are OPEN ; FB_SafeValve: bInverted FALSE - position feedback TRUE when the valve is open). Inputs xCmd (F-copy of the F-output), xFb, xReset ; cfg tEdm_ms 300. exp = NOT xCmd if bInverted else xCmd ; okfb = xFb = exp ; n = n+1 if NOT okfb else 0 ; rst = edge(xReset) (evaluated in EVERY call) ; if xError and rst and okfb: clear ; if NOT xError and n*100 >= tEdm_ms: xError, iAlarm 1 'feedback does not follow (welded / not switching)' ; xOn = xCmd AND okfb AND NOT xError.
_rules.FB_TwoHand: diagnostic mirror of the two-hand control (type IIIC: two 2-channel buttons, simultaneity 0.5 s - the F-program does the safety function). L = xLeft AND xLeft2 ; R = xRight AND xRight2 ; if NOT L and NOT R: blocked = FALSE, n = 0, xError = FALSE, iAlarm 0, xActuated = FALSE ; elif L <> R: n += 1 ; if n*100 > tSync_ms (500) and NOT xActuated: blocked = TRUE, xError = TRUE, iAlarm 1 'not simultaneous - release both' ; xActuated = FALSE ; else (both): xActuated = NOT blocked. Note the strict '>' : pressing the second hand in the 5th call after the first (500 ms) is still simultaneous.
_rules.FB_Scanner: safety laser scanner: qFieldA = iField = 1 ; qFieldB = iField = 2 (field-set switching by the standard program, the scanner checks the combination) ; xFree = xOssd1 AND xOssd2 ; xWarnOut = xWarn ; iAlarm = 0 if iField in {1,2} else 2 'invalid field set'.
_rules.FB_DoorLock: guard locking (item 7/8 DOOR_LOCK). C = xClosed AND xClosed2 ; L = xLocked AND xLocked2 ; nc/nl = discrepancy counters of the pairs ; if nc*100 >= tDisc_ms (500): xError iAlarm 1 'door switch discrepancy' elif nl*100 >= tDisc_ms: xError iAlarm 2 'lock switch discrepancy' ; if L and NOT C and NOT xError: xError iAlarm 3 'locked but not closed (tongue missing / manipulation)' ; if edge(xRequest) and C and L: xUnlockReq = TRUE (to the F-program: unlock after standstill) ; if NOT xClosed and NOT xClosed2: wasOpen = TRUE ; if xUnlockReq and wasOpen and C: xUnlockReq = FALSE, wasOpen = FALSE (door was opened and closed again -> request done, the F-program locks again) ; xClosedOk = C ; xLockedOk = L. (Errors are latched - cleared only by a new power-on / module reset in part B.)
_rules.FB_CmdIf: decision D1. Inputs iCntrlCmd, xCmdChangeRequest (data block, written by the cell controller), iState, iMode (from the module). e = edge(xCmdChangeRequest) ; iCmdExec = 0 ; if e: iLastCmd = iCntrlCmd ; if allowed(cmd, state, mode) (item 5 tables: EDGES with the command label, Stop from every state except Stopped/Stopping/Aborting/Aborted/Clearing, Abort from every state except Aborting/Aborted, and the command in MODES[mode], mode 1 Production / 2 Maintenance / 3 Manual): xCmdAck = TRUE, iCmdExec = iCntrlCmd (one call - the PackML core executes it) else xCmdRej = TRUE, iRejectCount += 1 (the MODULE program then sets Admin.WarningNo = M*1000 + 900 + iLastCmd - part B) ; if NOT xCmdChangeRequest: xCmdAck = xCmdRej = FALSE.
_rules.alarm_manager: decision D2 + D3. Each event (t, on/off, instance i, local alarm a): AlarmNo candidate = module_code*1000 + 10*i + a with the class from 'classes' for (FB type of instance i, a) ; instance i = 0 means the module itself (type 'MODULE'). Active list keeps the activation order. Admin.AlarmNo = the active class A or B alarm with the best (class, activation order) - A before B, earlier before later ; Admin.WarningNo = the earliest active class C ; AlarmClass for the signal tower = 1/2/3 of the most severe active (0 none) ; reaction = Abort (A), Hold if Execute (B), none (C). Log one line per event.
_rules.fb_library: the library = the 24 distinct FB types of item 9 codegen.fb_types (25 patterns; ANALOG_P and ANALOG_T share FB_AnalogIn) + FB_Safe2Ch, FB_Edm (bases) + FB_CmdIf, FB_AlarmMgr, function F_CmdAllowed (part A) ; FB_PackMLCore follows in part B. FB_MotorDol and FB_AnalogIn (+ limit alarm) keep the item 9 rules and tests (item9_examples.json motor / analog / limits). Wrappers: FB_Estop, FB_Door2Ch, FB_EnableSwitch, FB_LightCurtain = FB_Safe2Ch ; FB_SafetyCoupling = 2 x FB_Safe2Ch ; FB_ZoneOut, FB_ContactorPair = FB_Edm(bInverted TRUE) ; FB_SafeValve = 2 x FB_Edm(bInverted FALSE).

_input_defaults: see ref: Valve xPosA TRUE (starts at A), xEnable TRUE ; DriveSto xSto TRUE ; Heater rTemp 20.0, xTempGood TRUE, rSp 60.0 ; SignalTower iState 2 ; Feeder xSupplyOn TRUE ; Ups xUpsOk TRUE ; Edm xFb TRUE ; Scanner iField 1 ; DoorLock all four TRUE ; CmdIf iState 2, iMode 1 ; all others FALSE / 0.

fb_tests.name: S1 debounce: bounce ignored, 300 ms on / 200 ms off
V2 jam: B not reached -> alarm 1 -> reset -> retry ok
V3 lost position + both switches + disable
V4 bistable: disable holds, timer pauses
D1 STO release, run, STO stop, fault, reset
HS1 normal job then partner never busy
F1 breaker trips and comes back
U1 mains loss shorter and longer than the buffer time
E1 e-stop: power-on reset, press, reset, discrepancy
Z1 zone contactors follow, then one welds
W1 simultaneous, then too slow, then release
C1 4-phase command echo with accept and reject

alarm_manager._instances: M02 APC01 instances with an FB in item 8 expansion order (i = 1..5); module-level alarms use i = 0
alarm_manager._classes: (FB type, local alarm, class). FB_AnalogIn local alarms in this module: 1 'clamp pressure not reached in the clamp step' (B), 2 'clamp pressure lost while clamped in a machining state' (A), 3 'signal quality bad/uncertain' (C). MODULE 1 = 'not in home position' (decision D4). FB_AnalogIn itself only raises local alarm 3 (signal quality); alarms 1 and 2 are process alarms raised by the module program against the instance number of the analog input.
